summary: SKYTRACE – Infrared Sky Explorer is a web-based tool that makes NASA’s SPHEREx infrared sky observations easier to explore and compare over time. Users can search for selected astronomical targets or enter sky coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), retrieve available observations, and visualize prepared image cutouts through an interactive viewer. The platform supports time-based exploration, visual blinking, side-by-side comparisons, and a Change Receipt that records observation metadata, data provenance, and scientific limitations. By making complex infrared survey data more accessible, SKYTRACE aims to support citizen science, encourage collaborative exploration, and help users investigate potential changes in the sky without presenting unverified visual differences as confirmed astronomical discoveries.
details:
SKYTRACE – Infrared Sky Explorer is an interactive web application designed to make NASA’s SPHEREx infrared survey data accessible to citizen scientists, students, and astronomy enthusiasts.

Users can select from five challenge targets — Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis — or search using custom Right Ascension and Declination coordinates. The application queries available SPHEREx observations through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), retrieves observation data, and prepares image cutouts for visualization. Users can explore observations across different epochs using the viewer’s visual comparison features, including blinking and side-by-side viewing.

A key feature is the Change Receipt, which presents observation provenance, metadata, comparison information, validation status, and scientific limitations. It helps users distinguish exploratory visual differences from scientifically verified changes. This is particularly important because differences in wavelength coverage, image quality, detector characteristics, and calibration can affect how astronomical sources appear.

SKYTRACE aims to lower the barrier to exploring infrared astronomy data, encourage public participation in scientific discovery, and provide a transparent starting point for investigating possible moving or variable objects. It does not claim to confirm the discovery, identity, motion, or brightness variation of an astronomical object without the required scientific validation.

Tools and technologies: Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML, CSS, and NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx data services. The project uses a modular frontend and backend architecture, with API-based data retrieval, image preparation, and an interactive browser-based viewer.

The creative aspect of SKYTRACE is its combination of accessible visual exploration and a structured scientific provenance record. The team considered usability, data availability, observation metadata, image quality, wavelength differences, reproducibility, and the risk of false scientific interpretations while designing the application.
